The backends of `+ciphers::gcm+`, `+aes128_gcm+`, `+aes256_gcm+`, from the test programs that run it:

[cols="1,2,2,4",options="header"]
|===
|Backend |Jamfile |Header |Targets

|BearSSL
|`+/third_party//bearssl+`
|`+<webcpp/crypto/backends/bearssl.hpp>+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten (tested by `+gcm_bearssl+`, `+gcm_wycheproof_bearssl+`, `+agreement_gcm+`, `+agreement_gcm_portable+`)

|OpenSSL
|`+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+`
|`+<webcpp/crypto/backends/openssl.hpp>+`
|native, wasip2, wasip3 (tested by `+gcm_openssl+`, `+gcm_wycheproof_openssl+`, `+agreement_gcm+`, `+agreement_gcm_portable+`); not on emscripten: `+/webcpp/crypto//openssl+` stops the build there

|ctaes
|`+/third_party//ctaes+`
|`+<webcpp/crypto/backends/ctaes.hpp>+`
|refused at compile time (`+gcm_on_ctaes+`)
|===

`+aes128_gcm+` and `+aes256_gcm+` name the default backend. The default per target and what the program links, as <<crypto-backends-defaults>> gives it with its reasons and tests:

[.wrap-names,cols="2,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Target |Linked |Default

|emscripten
|BearSSL
|BearSSL

|wasip2, wasip3
|BearSSL, with or without OpenSSL
|BearSSL

|wasip2, wasip3
|BearSSL and OpenSSL, with `+WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL+`
|OpenSSL

|native, Clang and GCC
|OpenSSL, with or without BearSSL
|OpenSSL

|native, MSVC
|OpenSSL, with or without BearSSL
|OpenSSL

|native
|BearSSL and OpenSSL, with `+WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_BEARSSL+`
|BearSSL

|native
|BearSSL alone
|BearSSL
|===
